evidence.quote: An *Amazon EC2 managed instance* is an EC2 instance that is provisioned and managed by a designated service provider.

claim: A launch template stores launch parameters such as the AMI ID, instance type and network settings in numbered versions; when you launch without naming a version, the default version is used, and the default version is the first version unless you set another one.

values.display: the default version is used
values.spoken: without a version, the default version is used

values.display: it's the first version of the launch template
values.spoken: the default is the first version unless you change it

evidence.quote: For each launch template, you can create one or more numbered *launch template versions*. Each version can have different launch parameters. When you launch an instance from a launch template, you can use any version of the launch template. If you don't specify a version, the default version is used. You can set any version of the launch template as the default version—by default, it's the first version of the launch template.
For example, you can create a launch template that stores the AMI ID, instance type, and network settings that you typically use to launch instances.

note: d100. Launch configurations are blocked for accounts created on or after 2024-10-01: chapter 17 owns that fact (ec2-auto-scaling namespace).
